about: One complete CES flow on a simulated tenant, each step driving a real module screen: Muster collects the facts and writes the plan, Stamper applies it, AdminOps makes governed changes, and EvidenceOps assesses and proves it, with nothing reaching a real Microsoft tenant.

modules.name: Simulator
modules.blurb: A fictional Microsoft 365 GCC High tenant where every read and write lands, never a real one.

modules.name: Muster
modules.blurb: Collects the customer's facts and writes the Mission Plan.

modules.name: Stamper (Configuration)
modules.blurb: Applies the plan to the tenant and records what it did.

modules.name: EvidenceOps
modules.blurb: Assesses the tenant against CMMC Level 2, writes the SSP and the SPRS score, and keeps the evidence.

modules.name: AdminOps
modules.blurb: Runs approved admin commands through a governed pipeline and writes evidence for each one.

terms.meaning: A customer's own Microsoft 365 environment. Here it is simulated: nothing touches a real one.

terms.gloss: s1-mach (the fictional machine shop this demo uses)
terms.meaning: The simulated customer this demo uses: a fictional small machine shop.

terms.gloss: muster-api (the server behind the Muster screens)
terms.meaning: The server behind the Muster screens. It runs discovery, compiles the plan and sends it on.
Controlled Unclassified Information: government information a defense supplier must protect.

terms.gloss: Mission Plan (the plan Muster writes for the other modules to carry out)
terms.meaning: The plan Muster compiles. Stamper applies it; EvidenceOps assesses against it.

terms.gloss: SPRS (the Defense Department's Supplier Performance Risk System)
terms.meaning: The Defense Department's Supplier Performance Risk System, where a supplier reports its security score (110 at best).
Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification: the Defense Department's security standard for its suppliers. Level 2 has 110 practices.
AdminOps command New User Provisioning: adds a user the governed way.
AdminOps command Default User Permission Lockdown: stops ordinary users registering apps or creating groups and tenants.
System Security Plan: the document that says how each security requirement is met.

terms.gloss: Evidence Collector (the service that stores each upload with a tamper-evident fingerprint)
terms.meaning: The service that stores each uploaded document with a tamper-evident fingerprint (a hash).

terms.gloss: four-eyes rule (nobody reviews their own upload)
terms.meaning: Nobody reviews their own upload: a second person must.

terms.gloss: C3PAO (an accredited CMMC third-party assessment organisation)
terms.meaning: An accredited CMMC third-party assessment organisation: the outside assessor.

steps.title: Prepare the simulated tenant
steps.purpose: Check the simulated tenant (a customer's own Microsoft 365 environment) before anything runs.
steps.what: Checks that the simulator answers and serves s1-mach (the fictional machine shop this demo uses), makes sure every module reads the same tenant record, then opens the four module windows: Muster, Stamper, AdminOps and EvidenceOps.
steps.why: Every later step reads this one tenant. If one module looked at a different tenant, the numbers would not add up.
steps.value: Every number later in the demo traces back to one known tenant, so anyone can repeat the run.
steps.outputs: A record of each check and its result.
steps.manual: If the simulator serves another scenario, stop it, load the s1-mach scenario and start it again, as the runbook shows under "Start and stop each server". Prepare never restarts or reseeds a running simulator.

steps.title: The tenant we start from
steps.purpose: Show the starting point: a small, partly configured customer tenant.
steps.what: The Muster window shows a readout card from the simulator: it answers, and the tenant record carries a usable identity.
steps.expect: The card's last line names a multi-factor sign-in policy left in report-only mode. That wording belongs to a generic demo customer; on s1-mach the line reads the policy's real state.
steps.why: Everything after this is measured against this starting point: stamp, assess, change, assess again. CES never claims a change it cannot show.
steps.value: A known, fictional starting point: the whole flow can be shown and repeated without touching a real customer or real data.
steps.outputs: The readout facts and a screenshot of the card.
steps.manual: Open the simulator's address in a browser and check that its authorization policy answers.

steps.title: Sign in to Muster
steps.purpose: Sign in so muster-api (the server behind the Muster screens) records who acts.
steps.what: The Muster window opens the Discovery tab and signs in with the operator account. The signed-in state appears.
steps.why: Discovery, compile and push run on the server under a signed-in operator, so each action is recorded against a person.
steps.value: Every server action is tied to a named operator, which is what an audit trail needs.
steps.outputs: A screenshot of the signed-in state.
steps.manual: Open Muster, choose the Discovery tab, and sign in with the operator account that was created when muster-api was set up.

steps.title: Run discovery
steps.purpose: Let the machine read the tenant before anyone is asked a question.
steps.what: Muster types the tenant name on the Discovery tab and presses Run discovery. muster-api reads the simulated tenant, changing nothing, and marks each check met, not met or unknown. Then Muster continues.
steps.why: Facts the tenant can prove do not need to be asked. Discovery shortens the interview and drafts the CUI (Controlled Unclassified Information) boundary.
steps.value: Fewer questions for the customer: what the tenant can prove is read, not asked, which saves time and avoids answers from memory.
steps.outputs: A screenshot of the result, how long discovery took, and how many boundary drafts it made.
steps.manual: On the Discovery tab, type the tenant name, press Run discovery, wait for the result, then press Continue.

steps.title: Confirm the CUI boundary
steps.purpose: A named person confirms where CUI is stored and handled.
steps.what: Muster fills in the confirmer's name, confirms or corrects each boundary draft to match the customer's own answers, downloads the boundary record, and continues.
steps.why: The machine can infer; only a person can attest. The boundary decides which controls apply, so it must carry a name.
steps.value: A signed scope decision: the first thing an assessor asks for, and the basis for which controls apply.
steps.outputs: The downloaded boundary record, a screenshot, and each decision made.
steps.manual: On the boundary panel, type the confirmer's name, confirm or correct each draft, press Download record, then Continue.

steps.title: Describe the organisation
steps.purpose: Record who the organisation is, what it runs, and who is assessing.
steps.what: On the Situation screen Muster fills in the organisation profile, ticks the services in scope, and fills in the session details: tenant, tenant kind, operator. It does not press Begin Interview yet.
steps.why: The Mission Plan (the plan Muster writes for the other modules to carry out) is written for these services and this organisation.
steps.value: The plan fits this customer's services instead of a generic checklist, and the record shows who assessed what.
steps.outputs: A screenshot, and the values read back from the screen.
steps.manual: On the Situation tab, fill in the profile, tick the services, and fill in the session fields.

steps.title: Run the interview
steps.purpose: Ask only what discovery could not answer.
steps.what: Muster presses Begin Interview and types each answer from the customer's answer file, tab by tab. Answers discovery already settled are kept. A question the file does not answer gets "I don't know".
steps.why: An honest unknown beats a guess: it shows up as a gap to close, not as a false pass.
steps.value: The customer's score and plan are honest from the start, because gaps show up as gaps.
steps.expect: Leave the Muster window alone between steps: the next step presses Finish & Score. If it was pressed by hand, step 7 still exports the result.
steps.outputs: A screenshot, and which answers were typed, kept from discovery, or answered "I don't know".
steps.manual: Press Begin Interview and answer each question card; choose "I don't know" where the customer has no answer.

steps.title: Finish and export the readiness result
steps.purpose: Close the interview and get the customer's readiness number.
steps.what: Muster presses Finish, shows the score, and exports the readiness result, the status payload and the evidence package. Then it opens the Readiness tab and downloads its result.
steps.why: The number the customer reports to SPRS (the Defense Department's Supplier Performance Risk System) comes from the exported file, not the screen.
steps.value: The customer gets a readiness number and files they can keep or share, not just a screen.
steps.outputs: The readiness result, status payload and evidence package downloads, the score facts, and screenshots.
steps.manual: Press Finish, then each Export button, then open the Readiness tab and download the result.

steps.title: Compile the Mission Plan
steps.purpose: Turn the collected facts into the plan the other modules carry out.
steps.what: On the Plan tab Muster attaches the organisation file and presses Compile. muster-api reads the tenant again, changing nothing, and writes the Mission Plan and two files describing the tenant. Then Muster downloads the CUI boundary and the answers sent.
steps.why: One compiled plan is the single source that Stamper, AdminOps and EvidenceOps work from.
steps.value: One plan drives configuration, admin changes and evidence, so the modules never disagree about what was promised.
steps.outputs: The compile summary, the CUI boundary and answers downloads, and a screenshot.
steps.manual: On the Plan tab, choose the organisation content file, press Compile, wait for the result, then use the download buttons.

steps.title: Send the plan to Stamper and EvidenceOps
steps.purpose: Hand the plan over.
steps.what: Muster presses Send to Stamper. muster-api delivers the plan to Stamper and to EvidenceOps, and Muster shows what was sent.
steps.why: From here the plan is what gets applied and what gets assessed. Muster's job, collecting facts and writing the plan, is done.
steps.value: No re-keying between tools: the plan arrives in Stamper and EvidenceOps exactly as written.
steps.outputs: What was sent, and a screenshot.
steps.manual: On the Plan tab, press Send to Stamper and wait for the success message. muster-api must be started with CES_EO_URL and CES_EO_AUTH_TOKEN set, or the plan does not reach EvidenceOps.

steps.title: Translate the plan (Stamper)
steps.purpose: Turn the plan's instructions into concrete commands for this tenant.
steps.what: In the Stamper window the tenant is selected and connected, the plan just sent is loaded, the tenant is assessed, then the plan is translated into tasks. The task count appears at the bottom.
steps.why: Translation is where a plan becomes something a machine can run and a person can review, task by task.
steps.value: A person can review every concrete change before anything touches the tenant.
steps.outputs: Stamper screenshots (connected, assessed, translated) and the result card.
steps.manual: Open the Stamper console, select the tenant, connect, enter the paths of the plan and tenant manifest that were sent, press Assess, then Translate.

steps.title: Stamp the tenant (Stamper)
steps.purpose: Apply the plan to the tenant and prove each change.
steps.what: In the Stamper window the target is set to Tenant (never Dry Run), the plan is executed, and the run is followed to the end. The result is judged from Stamper's execution report, never from the badge.
steps.expect: One task is not applied: the leaver task (PS.L2-3.9.2, removing a departed employee). The leaver flow has no screen yet (a known issue, listed in KNOWN-ISSUES.md as KI-18). It is listed under Findings.
steps.why: Each command reads, changes, then reads again, so every change comes with its own evidence.
steps.value: Days of manual configuration become minutes, and every change carries its own before-and-after evidence.
steps.outputs: Stamper screenshots, the execution report and the result card.
steps.manual: In the Stamper console's Execute card, choose target Tenant, press Execute, and wait for Complete; the execution report is listed in the results.

steps.title: First assessment (EvidenceOps)
steps.purpose: Score the stamped tenant before AdminOps changes anything.
steps.what: In the EvidenceOps window the tenant is connected and all 110 CMMC (Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification) practices are assessed. Then the compliance matrix, one family's unmet rows and the SPRS score are shown, and saved as the before-state.
steps.why: A before and an after are how CES shows that a change moved a control, instead of asserting it.
steps.value: A measured starting score, so every later improvement can be shown rather than claimed.
steps.outputs: EvidenceOps screenshots and the before-state numbers.
steps.manual: Open the EvidenceOps console, select the tenant, press Connect, then Assess; open the dashboard and the SPRS tab.

steps.title: Add a user (AdminOps)
steps.purpose: Add a new user the governed way, with A-01 (New User Provisioning).
steps.what: In the AdminOps window A-01 is found, the tenant is picked, live execution is turned on, and the new user's name and sign-in name (fictional) are filled in. Then Execute.
steps.expect: Today this step stops before Execute: two read-only fields the form needs (licence and base group) are empty, because no screen writes them into the tenant record yet. It shows as not yet drivable.
steps.why: Admin changes go through one pipeline that checks, applies, checks again and writes evidence, so an assessor can see who changed what, and when.
steps.value: Routine joiner work goes through the same governed, evidenced pipeline as every other change, so daily admin keeps the tenant compliant.
steps.outputs: Screenshots of the form and the result, and the status and evidence outcome.
steps.manual: A-01 needs two read-only values the tenant record lacks: licence and base group (resources.m365LicenseSkuId, resources.baseGroupId), from the sent Tenant Manifest. No screen writes them yet. Once present: in AdminOps search A-01, open it, select the tenant, tick live execution, fill User Principal Name and Display Name, press Execute. Next phase, we will plan the missing screen with you.

steps.title: Make a governed change (AdminOps)
steps.purpose: Close a gap with A-18 (Default User Permission Lockdown), a governed command.
steps.what: In the AdminOps window A-18 runs live against the tenant: ordinary users can no longer register apps, create security groups or create tenants.
steps.expect: A-18 reads first and sets only what is not already set. On s1-mach the Stamper run already applied this setting, so A-18 confirms it and still records the evidence.
steps.why: This is the fix: a governed change with its own evidence record, ready for EvidenceOps to see.
steps.value: A fix is applied the same way every time and leaves its own evidence, which cuts remediation and audit preparation effort.
steps.outputs: Screenshots of the command form, the armed state and the result.
steps.manual: In AdminOps, search A-18, open it, select the tenant, tick live execution, press Execute.

steps.title: See the evidence record (AdminOps)
steps.purpose: Show what an AdminOps command leaves behind.
steps.what: In the AdminOps window the newer console opens, A-18 is chosen for the tenant, and Dry run is pressed. The evidence table shows the row it wrote: command, step, outcome, verdict, objectives and correlation id.
steps.why: Every dry run and every apply that reaches the server writes evidence. That trail is what EvidenceOps reads.
steps.value: The audit trail builds itself while the work is done; nobody collects screenshots afterwards.
steps.outputs: A screenshot of the evidence row and its details.
steps.manual: Open the newer AdminOps console (its app page), search A-18, select the tenant, press Dry run, and read the Evidence rows table.

steps.title: Re-assess and find what changed (EvidenceOps)
steps.purpose: Close the loop: show whether the change was captured.
steps.what: In the EvidenceOps window the tenant is assessed again, the control A-18 addresses (AC.L1-3.1.2) is compared with the before-state, and the SPRS score is shown. A flip is reported only when one really happened.
steps.expect: Stamper already met that control, so expect "no change". The SPRS score still moves, but not because of A-18: two controls count a prior assessment, and step 12 was the first (a known issue, listed in KNOWN-ISSUES.md as KI-25).
steps.why: Evidence of a fix is a before, an after, and the record between them. Saying "no change" when nothing changed is part of that honesty.
steps.value: Proof that a change was captured, or an honest "no change", keeps the score credible with an assessor.
steps.outputs: The before and after numbers, and a screenshot of the SPRS tab.
steps.manual: On the EvidenceOps console press Assess again, then compare the control's status with the first assessment and open the SPRS tab.

steps.title: Tenant and access (EvidenceOps)
steps.purpose: Show who may do what in EvidenceOps.
steps.what: In the EvidenceOps window the newer screens open, the tenant is selected, the operator token is entered (masked), and a short-lived uploader token is made for the named, fictional uploader.
steps.why: Uploads and reviews are tied to named people with short-lived tokens, so the evidence says who put it there.
steps.value: Every upload and every review traces back to a named person.
steps.outputs: A screenshot and the access facts.
steps.manual: Open the newer EvidenceOps screens on the Tenant and access tab, select the tenant, paste the operator token, type the uploader's sign-in name, press Mint uploader token.

steps.title: Generate the security plan (EvidenceOps)
steps.purpose: Produce the SSP (System Security Plan), the document an assessor reads first.
steps.what: On the SSP screen in the EvidenceOps window, Generate is pressed, then the Word document is downloaded.
steps.why: The SSP is written from the assessment and the evidence, not typed by hand, so it stays true to the tenant.
steps.value: The security plan is generated in minutes instead of written by hand, and it stays in step with the tenant.
steps.outputs: The SSP as a Word document, and its size.
steps.manual: On the SSP screen press Generate, wait for SSP generated, then press Export DOCX.

steps.title: Upload a document (EvidenceOps)
steps.purpose: Show evidence that no machine read can provide.
steps.what: On the Upload screen a short fictional document is uploaded, as the uploader, for a control no setting can prove (PE.L2-3.10.2). The Evidence Collector (the service that stores each upload with a tamper-evident fingerprint) keeps it.
steps.why: Some controls are met by documents and people, not settings. They still need evidence with a name and a fingerprint.
steps.value: Policy and people evidence sits next to the technical evidence, fingerprinted and attributed, ready for the assessor.
steps.outputs: The upload status and a screenshot.
steps.manual: On the Upload screen, type the control id and role, choose a file, press Upload, and check that the status names the uploader.

steps.title: Review the document (EvidenceOps)
steps.purpose: Show the four-eyes rule (nobody reviews their own upload) at work.
steps.what: First a reviewer token is made for the uploader, and the Review screen refuses: another person must review it. Then a token is made for a different fictional person, who records "met" for one objective.
steps.why: The screen enforces the rule, so a recorded review can be trusted.
steps.value: A reviewer's sign-off can be trusted because the system, not a policy document, enforces the four-eyes rule.
steps.outputs: Screenshots of the refusal and of the recorded review, and the review facts.
steps.manual: On Tenant and access, mint an approver token for the uploader and see the Review screen refuse; then mint one for the reviewer, choose the upload and objective, choose met, press Submit.

steps.title: Assess again and open the assessor view (EvidenceOps)
steps.purpose: Show how a reviewed document counts, as an assessor would see it.
steps.what: On the Assess screen the tenant is assessed again, then the Assessor view opens on the control's row.
steps.expect: One objective now has a met review. The control stays "not assessed" until every one of its objectives has a met review by someone other than the uploader.
steps.why: The assessor view is what a C3PAO (an accredited CMMC third-party assessment organisation) reads: each control, its status, and the evidence behind it.
steps.value: The customer sees the score the way an assessor will, before the assessment, so there are no surprises on the day.
steps.outputs: Screenshots, the score after the review, and the control's row.
steps.manual: On the Assess screen press Assess, wait for Evidence assessment complete, then open the Assessor view.

steps.title: Evidence Explorer (EvidenceOps)
steps.purpose: End where an assessor ends: the evidence itself.
steps.what: In the EvidenceOps window the assessment is shown (run again if the screen has none), then the compliance matrix, then the Evidence Explorer, which lists every evidence record, AdminOps ones included.
steps.why: Every score in CES points back to evidence someone can open. That is the end of this flow and the start of an assessment.
steps.value: Every score points to evidence an assessor can open, which shortens the assessment itself.
steps.outputs: EvidenceOps screenshots, ending on the Evidence Explorer.
steps.manual: On the EvidenceOps console, after an assessment, open the Evidence Explorer tab.

outOfScope: The leaver flow (removing a departed employee's access) has no screen yet (known issue KI-18). Next phase, we will plan it with you.
The prime and subcontractor rollup board is a different kind of engagement, not part of this flow.
